about.title: Edmond, Oklahoma — not Edmonds, Washington
about.content: Edmond Public Schools is the Central Oklahoma district headquartered on West Danforth Road in Edmond and serving the northern Oklahoma City metro, including some Oklahoma City and Logan County addresses inside EPS boundaries. The name is easy to confuse with Edmonds School District in Washington, but the two systems use different calendars, time zones and official websites. This page uses only sources from Edmond Public Schools in Oklahoma.

about.title: A 24,000+ student district with 31 schools
about.content: EPS currently presents itself as a district of more than 24,000 students and 31 schools. The district calendar is therefore a systemwide planning source: it covers the PK–12 opening, breaks, staff-development closures, conference periods and the scheduled end of school. Campus open houses, athletics, performances and bell-schedule changes still belong to the individual school's communication channels.

about.title: Weather planning is part of calendar planning
about.content: Central Oklahoma weather can change the meaning of a date after the PDF is published. EPS may choose remote learning or a non-instruction snow day, and the annual calendar says instructional time lost to inclement weather may be added to the end of the year. Families should keep the late-May window flexible and watch EPS text, app, website, social and local-media notices.

calendarNotes: Use the EPS instructional calendar for districtwide student dates, then use the assigned school's calendar for campus events and exact daily schedules. The annual PDF includes staff dates and office-status notes that do not always mean students attend. Parent-teacher conferences occur on different evenings for elementary, middle and high schools, so families should use the grade-level schedule rather than treating every conference date as districtwide. The reviewed 2026–27 PDF contains a January return-date and instructional-day-count conflict, which is disclosed on the school-year page. Weather closures may become remote-learning or non-instruction days and can change the planned ending. EPS generally avoids an early dismissal once the school day is underway because many students could reach an empty home. During tornado warnings, the district may hold students and buses until the all-clear rather than follow the normal dismissal time. An imported ICS file is a one-time snapshot and will not automatically receive later EPS revisions.

districtFaqs.q: Is this the Edmond or Edmonds school calendar?
districtFaqs.a: This is Edmond Public Schools in Edmond, Oklahoma, part of the Oklahoma City metro. It is not Edmonds School District in Washington. Verify the EPS name, Oklahoma location and edmondschools.net source before using these dates.

districtFaqs.q: Does every Edmond school use the district instructional calendar?
districtFaqs.a: The annual EPS calendar supplies districtwide attendance dates, breaks and staff-development closures. Individual schools still publish campus events, athletics, performances, open houses and detailed schedules, so families should use both the district calendar and the assigned school's communication.

districtFaqs.q: Where should Edmond families check school assignment and boundaries?
districtFaqs.a: Use the official EPS Boundaries page and its current elementary, middle and high school maps. EPS notes that families inside its boundaries may have Oklahoma City or Logan County addresses. Confirm the assignment before relying on a campus calendar or bell time.

districtFaqs.q: How does EPS announce weather-related schedule changes?
districtFaqs.a: EPS posts closures on district social channels and school websites, shares them with local media, and may send text and mobile-app notifications. The district tries to decide the evening before when possible, but rapidly changing Central Oklahoma weather can require a later decision.

districtFaqs.q: Does EPS dismiss early when severe weather develops?
districtFaqs.a: EPS says schools generally do not dismiss early for developing weather because many parents are working and students could arrive home to a locked house. During a tornado warning, students remain sheltered and buses may be held until the district gives the all-clear.
